title: One facade module is the sole reader of the pg client and opens on boot
description: The application accesses Postgres through a single facade module in the project's source tree that is the ONLY module in the tree that imports and reads the pg (node-postgres) client. Every other module that touches persistence imports the facade and calls its named domain verbs; no other module holds the raw pg client, a pg.Pool reference, or a pg.PoolClient reference. On process boot, the facade opens a pg.Pool against the elicited connection URL and, once the first successful ready-check completes, emits a facadeReady lifecycle event carrying the database name. The connection URL is elicited (project-config file by default; a security-secrets-management-applied project passes a secretRef). This blueprint declares the relationalStore applied capability against a project through this facade: any downstream blueprint whose requiresAppliedCapabilities lists relationalStore is satisfied by an applied persistence-data-postgres pinning the facade module to its Pool client and the elicited connection URL.
rationale: A single facade is what turns the raw pg driver surface into an application-side surface with domain-shaped verbs. Multiple call sites reaching into the driver directly produces a codebase where the shape of the store, the parameter-binding discipline, the event-emission discipline, and the pool posture are all diffused across the tree. One facade means one place to test, one place to swap (the round-6 Hyperdrive adapter slots in here without a facade re-shape), and one place where the persistence code paths are discoverable.
